answer: Reputation decay clocks. Each identity carries a public age counter that resets to zero whenever its transaction graph shows a sudden audience shift, detected via a prism of correlated counterparties. Mature identities earn fee discounts, so cloning forfeits that accumulated advantage. To farm fresh reputations, an attacker must run each clone through a slow meadow of low-value genuine interactions for months, paying real compute and fees per identity. The vault of earned discounts stays locked behind continuous honest history, making mass cloning costlier than one maintained account.
